name: Dak Ke Lake
kicker: The best-known lake on the plateau
summary: Get to Dak Ke in the first hour of light, while mist still sits on the water and the shore path is quiet. It is the best-known of Mang Den’s lakes: walk the shore, take a canoe out or fish where it is offered, and find the traditional nhà rông by the water. If you have one morning and want a waterfall, go to Pa Sy instead.
getThere: Short drive from Mang Den town
heroCaption: A waterlogged boat under blossom branches on Dak Ke lake

notice.title: The Pa Sy ticket does not cover this lake
notice.body: Pa Sy is a separate stop about 9 km from town, with its own gate.

body: Come early. The plateau is known for cloud at dawn, and Dak Ke is at its stillest before the day warms up. Walk the shore path under the trees, past old boats sitting low in the water, and look for the traditional nhà rông standing beside the lake.

Canoeing and fishing are offered on the lake. Ask at the shore what is running that morning. Then drive back through town, and spend the afternoon at Kon Pring on Highway 24 or on the 200 steps up to Khanh Lam pagoda.

Two quieter waters are nearby. The smaller Dak Ke waterfall is more remote, with a natural pool you can swim in once you reach it. The signs are poor, so ask in town for the path. Toong Dam is the still lake ringed by old trees, for a slower walk after Dak Ke.

figures.caption: Blossom branches over Dak Ke lake
figures.alt: Pink blossom branches in front of the green water of Dak Ke lake

gettingThere: Dak Ke is a short drive from the Mang Den town strip. Go by hired car, motorbike taxi, or rented motorbike, or ask your lodge for a driver. Pa Sy, the ticketed fall, is a different stop about 9 km from town.

legs.heading: From Mang Den town
legs.body: A short drive by car or motorbike.

legs.heading: From Kon Tum city
legs.body: About 60 km northeast up Highway 24 to Mang Den town by car or motorbike, then the short drive to the shore.

legs.heading: From Pleiku airport
legs.body: About 100 km by road to Mang Den town by hired car or taxi, then the short drive to the shore.

admissionNote: Ask at the shore about canoe and fishing charges. The Pa Sy ticket does not cover the lake.
